items.title: Meet Meta’s JiTTests: LLM-Generated Tests Designed to Fail Before Risky Code Lands
items.description:
Meta has moved Catching JiTTests into production. The LLM system writes tests designed to fail on risky diffs, and caught 74 privacy SEVs before landing in H1 2026, with a 60% engineer-reported true-positive rate.

The post
items.summary: Meta has implemented JiTTests, an LLM-generated testing system designed to fail on risky code changes, successfully identifying 74 privacy issues before they were merged in the first half of 2026. This initiative highlights efforts to enhance code safety and prevent potential data breaches by proactively catching problematic changes early in the development process.
items.summary_detailed: Meta has implemented JiTTests, an LLM-generated testing system designed to fail on risky code changes, preventing potential issues from being merged into production. In the first half of 2026, these tests identified and blocked 74 high-severity privacy vulnerabilities before they could be deployed, with a significant portion of flagged changes confirmed as true positives by engineers. This initiative significantly enhances Meta's ability to proactively address security risks in their codebase.
items.summary_bullets:
• Meta's JiTTests are LLM-generated tests.
• These tests fail on risky code changes.
• 74 privacy SEVs were caught before deployment.
• True-positive rate is reported at 60% by engineers.
